issues.legal_issue: The annual value of a building governed by rent-control legislation cannot exceed the standard rent determinable under that legislation, even when standard rent has not been fixed and the landlord may lawfully receive a higher contractual rent.
material_facts: The buildings were subject to rent-control legislation, but no standard rent had been fixed by the Controller.
Some buildings were let at contractual rents that could exceed the standard rent determinable under the rent-control legislation.
The municipal assessments used annual values exceeding the standard rent determinable under that legislation.
issues.conclusion: The annual value was limited to the standard rent determinable under the rent-control legislation and could not be based on a higher contractual rent.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 3(1)(b) of the Punjab Municipal Act, 1911 and section 116 of the Delhi Municipal Corporation Act, 1957, annual value is the rent at which a building may reasonably be expected to let. Rent-control legislation supplies an upper limit on that reasonable expectation, even where standard rent has not yet been fixed. The assessing authority may estimate the determinable standard rent for valuation purposes. The Court applied Corporation of Calcutta v. Life Insurance Corporation, [1970] 2 SCC 44, and Guntur Municipal Council v. Guntur Town Rate Payers' Association, [1971] 2 SCR 423; it relied on Corporation of Calcutta v. Padma Devi, [1962] 3 SCR 49, and distinguished Municipal Corporation, Indore v. Ratnaprabha, [1977] 1 SCR 1017, because the relevant municipal valuation provisions here had no non-obstante clause.

rule.if: municipal_house_tax_valuation_proceeding and rent_control_law_governs_building and standard_rent_not_fixed and assessed_annual_value_exceeds_determinable_standard_rent

predicates.municipal_house_tax_valuation_proceeding: A municipal authority assesses a building for house tax by determining its annual value.
predicates.rent_control_law_governs_building: Rent-control legislation applies to the building and provides for determination of a standard rent.
predicates.standard_rent_not_fixed: The authority empowered to fix the building's standard rent has not yet done so.
predicates.assessed_annual_value_exceeds_determinab: The assessed annual value is greater than the rent that can be determined by applying the rent-control legislation's standard-rent principles.

issues.definition: When a building is being valued for municipal house tax, rent-control legislation applies, standard rent has not been fixed, and the assessment exceeds the determinable standard rent, the annual value is limited to that determinable standard rent.

issues.legal_issue: An assessing authority may estimate standard rent for municipal valuation by applying the rent-control legislation's principles, without thereby fixing a standard rent binding on the landlord and tenant.
material_facts: Standard rent had not been fixed by the Controller for the buildings in issue.
The rent-control legislation set out principles for determining standard rent.
Determining annual value required the assessing authority to estimate the standard rent under those principles.
issues.conclusion: The assessing authority could determine its own estimate of standard rent for the purpose of assessing annual value; that estimate did not usurp the Controller's power to fix a binding standard rent.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 6 and 9 of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958 prescribe the principles and process for fixing standard rent. The assessing authority may apply those principles as part of the municipal valuation process, but its estimate is only for that purpose and is not a binding fixation of standard rent. The Court relied on Guntur Municipal Council v. Guntur Town Rate Payers' Association, [1971] 2 SCR 423, and treated the approach in Corporation of Calcutta v. Life Insurance Corporation, [1970] 2 SCC 44, as applicable. It also explained that section 9(2) does not give the Controller unfettered discretion to disregard the formula in section 6.

predicates.municipal_house_tax_valuation_proceeding: A municipal authority assesses a building for house tax by determining its annual value.
predicates.rent_control_law_provides_standard_rent_: The applicable rent-control legislation states principles for determining the building's standard rent.
predicates.standard_rent_not_fixed: The authority empowered to fix the building's standard rent has not yet done so.

issues.definition: Where a municipal valuation is being made, the rent-control legislation provides standard-rent criteria, and standard rent has not been fixed, the assessing authority may estimate standard rent for that valuation.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant's time bar from applying to fix standard rent does not raise the annual value above the determinable standard rent, and the same valuation limit applies to a self-occupied building.
material_facts: For tenanted buildings, the existing tenants were barred by limitation from applying to the Controller to fix standard rent, leaving them liable to pay the contractual rent.
The Court considered that a hypothetical tenant would not share the existing tenant's limitation bar and could seek fixation of standard rent after a hypothetical letting.
One appeal concerned a self-occupied building.
The applicable rent-control legislation provided principles for determining standard rent, although no standard rent had been fixed.
issues.conclusion: The limitation bar affecting an existing tenant did not justify valuing a building at the higher contractual rent, and annual value remained limited by determinable standard rent whether the building was tenanted or self-occupied.
issues.legal_principle: The statutory yardstick is the rent reasonably obtainable from a hypothetical tenant, not merely the amount the current tenant is legally obliged to pay. A hypothetical tenant is not subject to the current tenant's expired limitation period, and valuation should not vary according to whether the building is let or owner-occupied. The Court applied Guntur Municipal Council v. Guntur Town Rate Payers' Association, [1971] 2 SCR 423, and Corporation of Calcutta v. Life Insurance Corporation, [1970] 2 SCC 44; it considered M. M. Chawla v. J. S. Sethi, [1970] 2 SCR 390, concerning the operation of the rent-control prohibitions and limitation, but held that it did not determine the hypothetical letting value for municipal assessment.

rule.if: municipal_house_tax_valuation_proceeding and rent_control_law_governs_building and standard_rent_not_fixed and (existing_tenant_barred_from_fixation_application or building_is_self_occupied)

predicates.municipal_house_tax_valuation_proceeding: A municipal authority assesses a building for house tax by determining its annual value.
predicates.rent_control_law_governs_building: Rent-control legislation applies to the building and provides for determination of a standard rent.
predicates.standard_rent_not_fixed: The authority empowered to fix the building's standard rent has not yet done so.
predicates.existing_tenant_barred_from_fixation_app: The current tenant is prevented by a limitation rule from applying to have the standard rent fixed.
predicates.building_is_self_occupied: The owner occupies the building rather than letting it to a tenant.

issues.definition: In a municipal valuation proceeding involving a building governed by rent control where standard rent is unfixed, either the current tenant's inability to seek fixation or the owner's occupation of the building leaves the annual value limited to determinable standard rent.
